source: All-In Podcast — Anthropic $2T IPO, Zuck's AI manifesto, Nvidia $500B AI financing, Grok 4.6 / SpaceX AI strategy
summary: The primary risk to the AI capex supercycle is a compute glut/overbuild (dark GPUs), not demand destruction — but political headwinds ironically insure against this outcome
summary_extended: Baker argues that the primary bear case for the AI capex supercycle is not demand destruction but rather a 'dark fiber'-style compute glut — an oversupply of GPUs and data center capacity that crashes spot compute prices below the $30–50 per watt levels that have been underwritten by infrastructure investors. However, he contends this risk is structurally self-limiting because the same regulatory and political headwinds (permitting difficulties, grid interconnection delays, local opposition) that frustrate data center construction act as a natural governor on supply, preventing overbuild relative to exponentially growing AI compute demand. The irony, Baker notes, is that the political friction most view as a headwind actually insures the capex cycle against its own worst-case outcome. The investment implication is that the AI infrastructure buildout is more durable than bears expect, supporting continued investment in data center and power infrastructure plays.
